title: A deactivated technician's column keeps its work, shows inactive, stays pinned
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on the Work Orders build under test with Work Orders view permission; the Board View and Tech View display options are on.
  2. The current location has at least 3 lead technicians shown as groups/columns (a technician is eligible when they are Clockable, Active, and their role is not Office or Time Clock User).
  3. Via New Work Order, create several work orders and set a Lead Technician on each, spread across the technicians with some left Unassigned; then open the Work Orders page.
  4. A pinned technician who leads work is deactivated; in Board View.
custom_steps:
1. Pin a technician who leads work, then deactivate them.
  2. Switch to Board View.
  3. Confirm the work is still shown and the column shows an inactive indicator.
  4. Confirm the pin is retained.
  5. Manually unpin the deactivated technician and confirm it unpins.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Work led by a deactivated technician stays visible in that technician's column.
  • A deactivated technician's column shows an inactive indicator.
  • A technician keeps their pin after being deactivated.
  • You can manually unpin a deactivated technician.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043 (Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options). Story reference: SV-10046 — Story 3 Board View. Spec: Confluence page 845185030 “Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options (Draft Spec)”, Draft v0.9, requirement(s) S3-N2, S3-N4, S3-E3, S3-E5 (read 23 Sep 2026). Review decisions/answers: Confluence page 853901313 where cited. Source-verified on 23 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-N2: “Keep matching work visible in its deactivated technician’s column.”
  • S3-N4: “Show an inactive indicator on deactivated technician columns.”
  • S3-E3: “Retain a technician’s pin after deactivation.”
  • S3-E5: “Allow users to manually unpin deactivated technicians.”
